question: Ramesh sells an article for Rs. 34,440, after allowing an 18% discount on the marked price and still manages to gain 40% profit. If Ramesh sold the article at a 12% discount on the marked price, then what will be his profit, correct to two places of decimals?
solution:
**Given:**

Ramesh sells an article for ₹34,440 after allowing an 18% discount on the marked price and still manages to gain a 40% profit.

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹34,440

Discount = 18%

Profit = 40%

Cost Price (CP) = SP / (1 + Profit)

Marked Price (MP) = SP / (1 - Discount)

**Calculations:**

CP = 34,440 / (1 + 0.40)

⇒ CP = 34,440 / 1.40

⇒ CP = ₹24,600

MP = 34,440 / (1 - 0.18)

⇒ MP = 34,440 / 0.82

⇒ MP = ₹42,000

If Ramesh sold the article at a 12% discount on the marked price:

New SP = MP × (1 - 0.12)

⇒ New SP = 42,000 × 0.88

⇒ New SP = ₹36,960

New Profit = (New SP - CP) / CP

⇒ New Profit = (36,960 - 24,600) / 24,600

⇒ New Profit = 12,360 / 24,600

⇒ New Profit = 0.5024 = 0.5024 × 100 = 50.24%

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
